item.q: You missed your evening Spanish class, so you message a classmate. Ask politely, starting with *Could you tell me* or *Do you know*: 'Did the teacher give us any homework?'
item.why: *Did the teacher give us any homework?* becomes *if the teacher gave us any homework*: *if* (or *whether*), no *did*, and the verb in the past: *gave*.
item.why_lv: *Did the teacher give us any homework?* kļūst par *if the teacher gave us any homework*: *if* (vai *whether*), bez *did*, un darbības vārds pagātnē: *gave*.

r21b-4-039.gate_key: conj_linkers | B1.1 | gap | I finished work. ___, I went to the gym. |

accepted: After that

item.q: I finished work. ___, I went to the gym.
item.why: To introduce the next event, use *Then*, *After that* or *Afterwards*, not *After* on its own.
item.why_lv: Nākamo notikumu ievada ar *Then, After that* vai *Afterwards*, nevis ar *After* vienu pašu.
answers: After that

item.why_lv: *Although* + teikuma priekšmets + darbības vārds: pretstats (lija, tomēr mums patika).
answers: Although

r21b-4-043.gate_key: modal_verbs | B1.1 | mcq | Which sentence is NOT correct? | Tomorrow I will must work late.

wrong: You mustn't use your phone during the exam.

item.q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
item.why: *Must* has no past or future. Use *had to* or *will have to*.
item.why_lv: *Must* nav pagātnes ne nākotnes formas. Lieto *had to* vai *will have to*.
item.correct: Tomorrow I will must work late.
wrong: You mustn't use your phone during the exam.

answers: I will have to pay.
